data.body_html:
New Year's Eve on the Costa del Sol is a spectacle of light and celebration. While thousands pack the promenades of Puerto Banús and Marbella's Golden Mile, the smartest way to watch the midnight fireworks is from the deck of a private yacht. A Marbella yacht charter for NYE 2026 gives you front-row seats over the water, with your own bar, music, and space to dance. Here's everything you need to plan the night — boats, prices, tips, and logistics.

Why choose a yacht for NYE fireworks in Marbella?

The Marbella fireworks display at midnight is launched from the coastline between Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina. On land, you're competing for pavement space, queuing for drinks, and stuck with whatever view you can get. On a yacht, you anchor 200–500 metres offshore, looking directly up at the bursts. The sound echoes across the water, and you have total privacy.

With a licensed skipper handling the navigation, you can focus on your group. The boats are heated (or you can retreat to the cabin) and come stocked with cava, wine, beer, soft drinks, and snacks — all included in the price.

Best boats for NYE 2026: fleet overview

We offer two pricing tiers for NYE. Tier A boats are ideal for groups of 8–11, Tier B for those who want a larger, more luxurious experience. All depart from Puerto Banús.

For smaller groups, consider the Red Tide (6 pax) or Dubhe (5 pax) — pricing on request via WhatsApp.

What's included in your NYE charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% Spanish IVA. You also get unlimited water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. Tier B (Mangusta 80) adds a free jet ski — though you'll likely save that for daytime use.

You can bring your own food and decorations. Many clients order a catering platter from a Marbella deli or sushi from a Puerto Banús restaurant. The boat has a fridge, ice bucket, and basic glassware. Just no glass bottles on deck (plastic cups provided).

NYE 2026 timeline: what to expect

Fireworks are at midnight, but the night starts earlier. Here's a typical timeline for a 4-hour charter (21:00–01:00):

  • 21:00 – Board at Puerto Banús. Welcome cava and safety briefing.
  • 21:15–22:30 – Cruise along the coastline toward Marbella Marina. Views of La Concha mountain lit by the city lights.
  • 22:30–23:45 – Anchor in the bay. Music, drinks, snacks. Watch the land crowds build.
  • 23:55 – Countdown begins. Skipper will position the boat for the best view.
  • 00:00 – Fireworks. Toast with cava. Stay anchored for 20–30 minutes to enjoy the show.
  • 00:30–01:00 – Return to Puerto Banús.

For an 8-hour charter, you can start at 19:00, watch sunset at 18:15, then cruise to Cala del Faro or Cabopino before heading back for midnight.

How to book your NYE yacht charter

NYE 2026 is our busiest night. Slots for Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) and Tier B (Mangusta 80) typically sell out by mid-December. To secure your booking:

  1. Contact us via WhatsApp with your preferred boat and time.
  2. We'll check availability and send a quote (pricing on request for non-tier boats).
  3. Pay a 50% deposit to confirm. Balance due 7 days before the charter.
  4. Receive your boarding instructions and skipper details.

We recommend booking by November 2026 at the latest. For groups of 10–12, the Mangusta 80 or Azimut 58 Flybridge are the most popular choices.

What to wear and bring

December evenings in Marbella are mild but can feel chilly on the water. Air temperature is typically 13–17°C at night, and sea temperature is around 15°C. Wind chill on deck adds a few degrees of cold. Pack:

  • Warm jacket or fleece
  • Non-slip shoes (no high heels on deck)
  • Scarf and hat (optional but smart)
  • Sunglasses (sunset glare is strong)
  • Your own music playlist (bluetooth speaker onboard)
  • Camera or phone for photos

The boat's saloon and cabin are heated, so you can warm up between deck sessions.

Alternatives: daytime NYE cruises

If you prefer a quieter celebration, consider a daytime charter on 31 December. The weather is often sunny (16–18°C), and you can cruise to Estepona or Sotogrande. Rates are the same as standard daytime charters: Tier A from €749/2h. You'll be back at the marina by 17:00, leaving time for a land-based dinner.
